note: On macOS this Horizon build presents its frames in step with the 144 Hz display even with VSync off, so its average frame rate here is capped at 144: compare the 1% lows and frame times instead. The Mac mini was also running other jobs during the runs (CI, simulators; 1-minute load average 20 to 56 on 14 threads), which costs both games, vanilla more at render distance 32.

A 2016 laptop: 2 cores / 4 threads and Intel integrated graphics, Linux with Mesa 26.1.8 (Horizon on Vulkan, vanilla on OpenGL). It has no screen attached, so both games drew to a GPU compositor (sway on the Intel GPU) in a 1280x720 window. Horizon ran two flights per scene, vanilla two separate games of one. Render distance 32 is not shown: in 5 minutes neither game finished loading the spawn, and given 25, Horizon kept only about 900 to 1,400 chunk columns resident on this machine instead of the 3,200 a full view holds, so the two games would not have drawn the same world.

Linux (NixOS) with the NVIDIA 595 driver. The desktop is in daily use, so both games drew to a separate GPU compositor (a headless sway rendering on the RTX 4080) in a 1280x720 window, never on its screen: Horizon through Wayland, vanilla through Xwayland, both on Vulkan. Other jobs were running during the runs (1-minute load average 18 to 25 on 24 threads), which costs both games, chunk loading most.
